name: Competition Scoring Strategy
description: A rulebook-based observation guide to points, advantages and penalties in IBJJF competition.
summary: Distinguish scoring actions, stabilization and tiebreakers when reviewing an IBJJF match.
overview: A position name alone does not explain a score. The IBJJF rulebook specifies how an athlete gets there, what control is established and whether a submission interrupts the count. Start with an exchange whose scoreboard change you cannot explain, then identify the applicable article before judging the tactical choice.

guide.display_title: IBJJF Scoring: Read the Whole Exchange

fits: You know the headline point values but cannot always explain why a pass, reversal or near-finish did or did not score.
consider_alternative_if: For ADCC comparisons, use No-Gi Competition Approach; its scoring phases and positional values differ.

includes: A guard pass scores three points when its required control is established; arriving in side control without passing a guard is a different situation.
Article 3.4 permits cumulative points through continuous positional progression; its pass-to-mount example totals seven.
At regulation time, tied points are separated by advantages, then fewer penalties, then a referee decision if still tied.
limits: This guide selects scoring questions; the full rulebook covers additional exceptions and stoppage outcomes.
A camera angle may not show the details needed to explain a referee’s decision.

start_here.title: Explain one scoreboard change
start_here.task: Choose an IBJJF match recording you can pause. For one guard-passing exchange, note the starting guard, the resulting control, any submission interruption and the scoreboard change. Compare those observations with Articles 3 and 4.2. If the action continues directly to mount, check Article 3.4 before assuming separate pauses were required. Mark anything the camera cannot establish.

sources.title: IBJJF Rules Book
sources.note: Read point values, cumulative scoring, guard-pass conditions and the regulation-time tiebreak order. These provisions explain scoring rather than prescribe an attacking sequence.

flashcards.question: Under IBJJF rules, what is the regulation-time tiebreak order after equal points?
flashcards.answer: Compare advantages, then penalties: more advantages wins; if those are tied, fewer penalties wins. A remaining tie goes to the referee decision under Article 2.6.

flashcards.question: Under IBJJF Article 3.4, must a continuous guard-pass-to-mount sequence stop separately in both positions to score?
flashcards.answer: No. With continuous qualifying control through the sequence, the referee counts three seconds at the final scoring position and awards cumulative points; the rulebook’s example totals seven.

flashcards.question: Under IBJJF Article 4.2, does reaching side control always earn guard-pass points?
flashcards.answer: No. A guard must have been passed, followed by the required side or north-south control for three seconds, subject to the scoring rules.
flashcards.answer_line: No; a guard must be passed
